references.text: It contains the same command about just weights and measures, where God commands that the Israelites should have accurate weighing stones, ephah and hin.
A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a full weight is His delight - expressing the same principle of honesty in trade.
Accurate weights and balances are from the Lord - confirming that just measures are part of God's order.
Two kinds of weighing stones and two kinds of ephah are both an abomination to the Lord - warning against dishonesty in trade.
The prophet Ezekiel commands a just weight, a just ephah and a just bath - repeating the requirement for honesty in measures and weights.
The prophet Amos accuses those who make the ephah small and the shekel large and falsify the scales - showing the consequence of breaking this command.
The prophet Micah condemns false weights and deceitful balances as injustice that the Lord cannot accept.
The promise to prolong days in the land is linked to honoring parents; the same promise is given here for honesty in trade.
The promise of long days in the land which the Lord your God gives you - the same blessing for obedience to God's commands.
